question: A fuse works on the principle of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Heat produced by electric current.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **fuse** works on the **principle of heat** produced by electric current.
 
• A fuse is an **electrical safety device** that protects an **electrical circuit** from damage caused by **overloading or short-circuiting.**
 
• It consists of a** metal wire or filament** that melts when the current flowing through it exceeds a certain limit, thus breaking the** circuit and preventing further damage.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Light produced by electric current: **This principle is used in **incandescent bulbs,** where a filament is heated by the electric current to produce light.
 
• **Magnetic effect produced current: **This principle is used in **electromagnets, **where a current passing through a coil of wire produces a magnetic field.
 
• **Heat absorbed by electric current: **This is not a principle that is used in any electrical device, as it goes **against the laws of thermodynamics.**
 
• Heat is always produced when **current flows through a wire,** not absorbed.
